name: The men of Gibeah, and Benjamin
charge: Sodomy, gang rape and murder of a stranger's concubine; a tribe that shielded the guilty
summary: The men of Gibeah surrounded the house where a Levite lodged, demanding him; they were given his concubine and abused her all night until she died on the threshold. He cut her into twelve pieces and sent them through Israel. Benjamin refused to surrender the guilty, and Israel went to war.
offense: The Levite passed by Jebus because he would not lodge in a city of strangers and chose Gibeah, a city of Benjamin. Yet no man there first received him, and an old man from Mount Ephraim brought the travellers into his house (Judges 19:10-21). The guest expected safety among brethren; the city's conduct betrayed that expectation. Men surrounded the house and demanded the male guest, as the men of Sodom had demanded Lot's visitors (Judges 19:22; Genesis 19:4-9). The woman was brought out to them, and they raped and abused her through the night. She fell at the door with her hands upon the threshold and gave no answer when her husband spoke (Judges 19:25-28). This was violence against her, not consent. Deuteronomy 22:25-26 places the guilt of forced intercourse upon the attacker and compares the assault to a man rising against his neighbour to slay him. The Levite sent the evidence throughout Israel, and the congregation assembled as one man. They demanded that Benjamin surrender the perpetrators so that evil could be put away (Judges 19:29-30; 20:1-13). Benjamin refused and gathered to fight its brethren (Judges 20:14). The tribe made itself the defence of the guilty. Loyalty to one's own becomes transgression when it shields the crime instead of submitting the offenders to judgment.
judgment: Israel brought four hundred thousand swordsmen against Benjamin, yet lost twenty-two thousand men on the first day and eighteen thousand on the second (Judges 20:17-25). Numbers and indignation did not secure victory. Israel had enquired of the Lord, but the express promise of deliverance came after the whole congregation wept, fasted, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before him (Judges 20:26-28). They had to humble themselves as well as prosecute the wickedness among their brethren.

entries.commentary: Once more, there was no king in Israel, no leadership structure, still sheep without a shepherd. A certain Levite sojourning on the side of mount Ephraim took to him a concubine out of Bethlehemjudah; a concubine was a woman dealt with on the level of a servant. His concubine played the whore against him, laid with another man, then went away from him unto her father's house to Bethlehemjudah and was there four whole months.

Instead of letting her go, her husband arose and went after her to speak friendly unto her and to bring her again, with his servant and a couple of asses, and the damsel's father rejoiced to meet him. By the law, a woman who is put away and becomes another man's is defiled to her former husband, and taking her back defiles the land. The Most High does not permit it, but with no king in the land and no enforcement of the law, this is what men did.

The damsel's father retained him: eat, drink, lodge, three days, then a fourth, then a fifth. Like an old man who never has anybody to talk to, he kept finding a reason not to let the Levite go, and a one night plan stretched into five days. The father's words on the fifth day cut a popular doctrine. They tarried until afternoon, and he said, behold, the day draweth toward evening, and then, behold, the day groweth to an end. According to the Bible the day ends at evening; and if it ends at evening it begins at evening, so a day runs from evening to evening, including the sabbath. That buries the sunrise to sunrise doctrine, which has no works and no fruits to show it was ever right.

The man would not tarry that night; five days was enough and he had business to tend to. He rose up, departed, and came over against Jebus, which is Jerusalem, with two saddled asses and his concubine. Jerusalem is called Jebus here because the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of Jerusalem, still dwelt in it; this is before David rose up and took it from them. When Israel came out of the wilderness, the promised land was inhabited primarily by Canaanites, and the children of Judah could not drive the Jebusites out.

The sun went down upon them by Gibeah, which belongeth to Benjamin, and when they went in and sat down in a street of the city, no man took them into his house to lodge. The Benjamites were not so friendly. An old man from his work out of the field at even, a man of mount Ephraim sojourning in Gibeah, lifted up his eyes and questioned the wayfaring man: whither goest thou? and whence comest thou? The Levite explained he was passing toward the house of the LORD with straw, provender, bread, and wine of his own, lacking nothing, yet no man would receive him to house. The old man said, peace be with thee; howsoever let all thy wants lie upon me; only lodge not in the street. He knew the manner of the men of that city and what the streets of Gibeah held at night. He brought them into his house, and they washed their feet and did eat and drink.

As they were making their hearts merry, certain sons of Belial, meaning children of the devil, demon seed, beset the house round about and beat at the door in the middle of the night, saying to the master of the house, bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him. To know in this context is sexual intercourse; the men of Gibeah were howling for the man himself. This is a rerun of a very familiar story of old, the men of Sodom at Lot's door, and the scripture names exactly what vile thing they were after.

The men would not hearken, so the man brought his concubine forth unto them; and they knew her, and abused her all the night until the morning. They is plural: this was a gang rape, forced, nothing voluntary about it, done in the anger of men who could not get the man they wanted. When the day began to spring they let her go, and the woman came in the dawning of the day and fell down at the door of the man's house where her lord was, her hands upon the threshold. In the morning he said, up, and let us be going; but none answered. There was no more spirit left in her; she was dead. He laid her upon an ass and got him unto his place. What we witnessed is rape, and the scripture is plain that rape is a sin worthy of death; marriage is the only honorable bed. Men out here calling themselves Israelites and teaching otherwise give Israelites a bad name; we preach the laws of the Most High.

When he was come into his house he took a knife, laid hold on his concubine, and divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel, to make the twelve tribes aware of what was done in Gibeah. All that saw it said, there was no such deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider of it, take advice, and speak your minds. The nation had never seen a matter like this, and it called the whole congregation to counsel.

All the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the LORD in Mizpeh: four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword. Israel got ready for war behind one woman, one victim. There is no hatred of women in this truth; wicked women are rebuked, which is itself love, and here a crime against one sister moved the whole nation to arms.

The children of Benjamin heard that Israel was gone up to Mizpeh. The Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, testified: I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, and the men of Gibeah rose against me and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me; and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead. Forced is the Bible's word for rape. He said they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel. Nowhere in the Bible can rape be called lawful; it is lewdness and folly, and whether the victim lives or dies the matter is counted as murder. Be very mindful of sick, perverted camps that teach otherwise.

All the people arose as one man, saying, we will not any of us go to his tent, neither will we any of us turn into his house; none of us are going home until this is answered. They set an order for war, ten men of an hundred throughout all the tribes to fetch victual for the people, and all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man. Even wicked and without a king, Israel had some morals left; gang rape was intolerable.

The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, what wickedness is this that is done among you? Now deliver us the men, the children of Belial which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and put away evil from Israel; everything those men had going on was worthy of death. But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren; instead they gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah to go out to battle against the children of Israel, riding for their own no matter the crime.

Benjamin numbered twenty and six thousand men that drew sword out of the cities, beside the inhabitants of Gibeah, seven hundred chosen men. Among all this people were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded, every one able to sling stones at an hair breadth and not miss: slinging with the velocity of a firearm and dead accurate. Benjamin was about that action. The men of Israel beside Benjamin were four hundred thousand men of war that drew sword. Four hundred thousand against twenty and six thousand: you would think a landslide victory.

The children of Israel arose, went up to the house of God, and asked counsel of God: which of us shall go up first to the battle against the children of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first. Israel encamped against Gibeah and put themselves in array, and the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground of the Israelites that day twenty and two thousand men. Benjamin opened the battle by giving Judah the business.

The men of Israel encouraged themselves; we cannot go out like that to the men of Gibeah. They set their battle again in array in the same place, went up and wept before the LORD until even, and asked, shall I go up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the LORD said, go up against him. The second day Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground eighteen thousand more, all men that drew the sword. Fresh legs came in against them and Benjamin still had the endurance and stamina to whip them.

Then all the children of Israel and all the people went up unto the house of God, wept, sat there before the LORD, fasted that day until even, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD. This time the whole nation humbled itself. The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it. They asked, shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand: a direct promise of victory on the morrow.

Now Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah. No more going head up against lefthanded slingers you cannot beat straight on; now there was a strategy, an ambush. Part of Israel put themselves in array as at other times, and Benjamin was drawn away from the city, beginning to smite and kill about thirty men and saying, they are smitten down before us as at the first. Little did they know they were falling into the plan; Israel fled on purpose and drew them from the city onto the highways. The liers in wait came forth out of their places, even out of the meadows of Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel: the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men. The victory belonged to the Most High, as he had promised.

There was an appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city. That was the purpose of drawing the Benjamites out: while Benjamin smote about thirty men and thought they were winning as in the first battles, the liers in wait hasted, rushed upon Gibeah, smote all the city with the edge of the sword, and set the sign. When the flame began to arise out of the city with a pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them, and behold, the flame of the city ascended up to heaven; and the men of Benjamin were amazed, for they saw that evil was come upon them. In that moment they knew it was over. They turned their backs before the men of Israel unto the way of the wilderness, toward the rock of Rimmon, but the battle overtook them: eighteen thousand men of valour fell, five thousand were gleaned in the highways, and two thousand slain at Gidom, twenty and five thousand in all, including all those mighty lefthanded men of valour.

Six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon and abode there four months; only that remnant kept the tribe from being utterly destroyed. The men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin and smote them with the edge of the sword, men of every city, and beast, and all that came to hand, and set on fire all the cities they came to. Benjamin was judged big time; the Most High pushed the reset button on the tribe for the sodomite and rape activity that came out of Gibeah. Chapter 21 shows the drastic measures that had to be taken so Benjamin could continue producing as a tribe. That judgment is why Saul, in the days of the first king, calls himself a Benjamite of the smallest of the tribes of Israel; this war is what minimized the tribe. There have been mighty and righteous Benjamites since, Paul chief among them, but it is written, and we learn the history as it is written.

The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh that not one of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife. This follows the previous chapter, where the tribes went to war against Benjamin. The people came to the house of God and sat there till evening before God, lifted up their voices and wept sore, asking why it had come to pass that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel. The next day they rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. The children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, for there was one tribe cut off from Israel that day. They had also made a great oath that whoever came not up to the Lord at Mizpeh would surely be put to death.

The question of the chapter: how shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord not to give them our daughters? They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and the law says a sworn oath must be performed; that is why they could not simply turn around and give their daughters.

They searched which tribe came not up to Mizpeh, and behold, none had come from Jabeshgilead to the assembly. So under the great oath the congregation sent twelve thousand of the valiantest men to smite Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, destroying every male and every woman that had lain by man. Among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead they found four hundred young virgins that had not known man by lying with any male, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan. Verse 12 is the precept for what it means in scripture to know somebody: to lie with them, meaning to have sex with them.

The whole congregation sent to speak peaceably to the children of Benjamin at the rock Rimmon, and Benjamin came again. They gave them the wives saved alive of the women of Jabeshgilead, but they sufficed not; there were not enough for all the men that remained. The people repented them for Benjamin because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel, and the elders said there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel. Verse 18 restates why they could not just give their own daughters: the children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin. That is the same oath read in verse 7.

The solution: there was a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, so they commanded the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards, and when the daughters of Shiloh came out to dance in the dances, every man was to catch him a wife of the daughters of Shiloh and go to the land of Benjamin. When the fathers or brethren came to complain, the elders would answer, Be favourable unto them for our sakes; because the fathers did not give their daughters, they would not be guilty of breaking the oath. The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number of them that danced, then returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them.

The children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, to his family, and to his inheritance. In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes. We see that same thing today: most of our people are still in that state, doing what is right in their own eyes. There is nothing new under the sun. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)
Lot sat in the gate and pressed the two angels into his house, because he knew the men of Sodom. He made them a feast, and they did eat; angels have bodies and functions like men.

The men of Sodom, old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed the house and demanded the men, that we may know them. To know in scripture is to lie with: Rebekah was a virgin, neither had any man known her. The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness.

Lot went out and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. This is Genesis, way before [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18); sodomy was already wickedness and already unlawful before the law was written at Sinai. They pressed on Lot to break the door, and the angels smote them with blindness, small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

Lot's sons in law took him as one that mocked, and they perished. When the warning comes, treating it as a joke is death. While Lot lingered, the angels laid hold on his hand, the Lord being merciful to him. Then the instruction: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee; escape to the mountain.

The angel told Lot, Haste thee, for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. The destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, the same way the angels in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7) hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed. When Lot entered Zoar, the Lord rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. Those cities are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire; what was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands. Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.

Lot's wife looked back, against the instruction, and became a pillar of salt: a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.

Lot's daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and no man was left on the earth to give them seed, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him; he perceived not when they lay down nor when they arose. Do not take any wayward idea from this: uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now. The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.

verses.text: Now as they were making their hearts merry, behold, the men of the city, certain sons of Belial, beset the house round about, and beat at the door, and spake to the master of the house, the old man, saying, Bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him.
And the man, the master of the house, went out unto them, and said unto them, Nay, my brethren, nay, I pray you, do not so wickedly; seeing that this man is come into mine house, do not this folly.
Behold, here is my daughter a maiden, and his concubine; them I will bring out now, and humble ye them, and do with them what seemeth good unto you: but unto this man do not so vile a thing.

But the men would not hearken to him: so the man took his concubine, and brought her forth unto them; and they knew her, and abused her all the night until the morning: and when the day began to spring, they let her go.
Then came the woman in the dawning of the day, and fell down at the door of the man’s house where her lord was, till it was light.

And her lord rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way: and, behold, the woman his concubine was fallen down at the door of the house, and her hands were upon the threshold.
And he said unto her, Up, and let us be going. But none answered. Then the man took her up upon an ass, and the man rose up, and gat him unto his place.
And when he was come into his house, he took a knife, and laid hold on his concubine, and divided her, together with her bones, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel.

And it was so, that all that saw it said, There was no such deed done nor seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land of Egypt unto this day: consider of it, take advice, and speak your minds.
And the Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, answered and said, I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge.
And the men of Gibeah rose against me, and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me: and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead.
And I took my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the country of the inheritance of Israel: for they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel.
Behold, ye are all children of Israel; give here your advice and counsel.
And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, What wickedness is this that is done among you?

Now therefore deliver us the men, the children of Belial, which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel. But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel:
And the Lord smote Benjamin before Israel: and the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men: all these drew the sword.
So that all which fell that day of Benjamin were twenty and five thousand men that drew the sword; all these were men of valour.
But six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon, and abode in the rock Rimmon four months.

And the men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword, as well the men of every city, as the beast, and all that came to hand: also they set on fire all the cities that they came to.
And the people came to the house of God, and abode there till even before God, and lifted up their voices, and wept sore;
And said, O Lord God of Israel, why is this come to pass in Israel, that there should be to day one tribe lacking in Israel?
They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah: therefore he will remember their iniquity, he will visit their sins.
O Israel, thou hast sinned from the days of Gibeah: there they stood: the battle in Gibeah against the children of iniquity did not overtake them.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.

And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, What wickedness is this that is done among you?

Now therefore deliver us the men, the children of Belial, which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel. But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel:
And the Lord smote Benjamin before Israel: and the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men: all these drew the sword.
So that all which fell that day of Benjamin were twenty and five thousand men that drew the sword; all these were men of valour.
But six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon, and abode in the rock Rimmon four months.

And the men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin, and smote them with the edge of the sword, as well the men of every city, as the beast, and all that came to hand: also they set on fire all the cities that they came to.
And the people came to the house of God, and abode there till even before God, and lifted up their voices, and wept sore;
And said, O Lord God of Israel, why is this come to pass in Israel, that there should be to day one tribe lacking in Israel?
They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the days of Gibeah: therefore he will remember their iniquity, he will visit their sins.
O Israel, thou hast sinned from the days of Gibeah: there they stood: the battle in Gibeah against the children of iniquity did not overtake them.
But before they lay down, the men of the city, even the men of Sodom, compassed the house round, both old and young, all the people from every quarter:
And they called unto Lot, and said unto him, Where are the men which came in to thee this night? bring them out unto us, that we may know them.
